newsitem.title: GERMANY: AGFA GEVAERT TO CUT BELGIAN, GERMAN JOBS.
newsitem.headline: AGFA GEVAERT TO CUT BELGIAN, GERMAN JOBS.

text.p: Agfa Gevaert, the photographic film and products unit of German chemicals giant Bayer AG , said on Tuesday it plans further redundancies at its German and Belgian operations by the end of 1997.
Agfa said that around 550 workers out of the current 6,400 would lose their jobs in its German operations end-1997.

Agfa was seeking further redundancies in Belgium, where the current job-cutting programme calls for 1,000 redundancies between 1994 and 1996. There are 6,300 employees at Agfa's Belgian operations at the moment.
The job cuts come as part of a rationalisation process aimed at streamlining the company, Agfa said in a statement.
Management board chairman Klaus Gerlach said the cut-backs in the number of employees and efficiency-improving plans would help streamline costs.
Improving efficiency was also behind moves to centralise the management board at Mortsel in Belgium. Currently its activities are divided between Mortsel and Leverkusen.
The rationalisation programme aims to double return on revenues by 1998 from their current levels of three percent.
